key_insight: Func-R1 shows that multimodal math errors often come from visual-text interference, so the model must jointly preserve visual evidence and symbolic function reasoning.
engineering_relevance: The paper offers a practical post-training recipe for improving function-based reasoning in MLLMs, which is useful for building more reliable STEM vision-language systems.
method: Use an explicitly decoupled architecture to separate perception from reasoning.
Apply hierarchical post-training to first identify critical visual cues, then perform deeper theoretical reasoning.
Introduce Perception-Aligned Theoretic Optimization (PATO) to update the policy while correcting visual information during reasoning.
evidence_signal: The authors report strong gains across diverse benchmarks, including an 8.4% improvement over GPT-5 on MathVerse function-oriented tasks.
watch_item: Results may depend on careful coordination between perception and reasoning stages, so the decoupled training and PATO pipeline could be sensitive to implementation details and benchmark-specific visual cues.
paper_title: Func-R1: Incentivizing Mathematical Function Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
